CAR@GB.text: Packers EDGE Micah Parsons and C Sean Rhyan won't be available Thursday against Carolina.

ARI@DAL.text: The 2-5 Cardinals are 8-2 against the spread in their last 10 meetings with Dallas. The Cowboys love giving them a touchdown head start anyway.

ATL@TB.text: The Bucs are 0-4 against the spread at home and 0-2 as favorites. So naturally, Vegas has them favored at home.

BAL@BUF.text: Lamar Jackson is back with no injury tag after missing three games, and Baltimore went 1-2 without him. So much for Buffalo's relaxing bye.

CLE@PIT.text: The Browns are 5-2 with a -13 point differential, tied for the fourth-worst for a 5-2 team since 2000. Ugly wins still count, Pittsburgh.

IND@JAX.text: The Colts have lost three straight and managed 10 points last week at Minnesota. Jacksonville is laying 10. Bold ask of that offense.

LV@NYJ.text: Kirk Cousins leads the NFL with 16 TD passes. Yes, that Kirk Cousins. The Raiders have still lost four straight.

MIN@DET.text: The 6-0 Vikings have allowed a league-low 74 points and hit the Under five straight. Lions games are 5-1 to the Over. Something's gotta give.

TEN@CIN.text: Joe Burrow: 15 TD passes, 3 picks. The 1-6 Titans get 12.5 points; Cincy is 8-2 against the spread in the last 10 meetings.

LAC@LA.text: The Chargers are 0-6 and 0-5-1 against the spread. They can't even lose by the right amount.

KC@DEN.text: Denver is 7-3 against the spread in the last 10 meetings with KC, yet the Broncos are home underdogs. Mile High calls that disrespect.

NE@MIA.text: Miami finally won a game last week. The 1-5 Dolphins are also 8-2 against the spread in the last 10 meetings with New England.

PHI@WAS.text: Tanner McKee starts for Philly in the first post-September Sunday night game since 2006 with a combined win percentage under .300. Prime time!

CHI@SEA.text: The Bears are 5-2 against the spread, best in the NFL, and have covered every game Caleb Williams started and finished. Seattle, you've been warned.

JAX@BAL.text: Lamar Jackson is out and third-stringer Joe Fagnano starts. Vegas noticed: Baltimore went from lookahead favorite to a 10-point home dog.

CIN@ATL.text: Joe Burrow leads the NFL at 302.1 passing yards a game. Michael Penix Jr. ranks 32nd of 35 starters in completion % over expected. Olé.

CLE@NO.text: The 2-5 Saints have yet to win a home game this season, and Vegas still has them favored over the 5-3 Browns.

DAL@IND.text: The Colts have lost four straight, including a 42-7 beatdown in Jacksonville. Dallas has dropped three of four. Somebody has to win this.

DEN@CAR.text: The Broncos are 4-0 against the spread as favorites. Carolina's run defense ranks 28th in yards per carry allowed. Yikes.

DET@MIA.text: The 1-6 Dolphins are 0-3 at home, and Jahmyr Gibbs just ran for 153 yards. Hard Rock, meet hard running.

LA@WAS.text: The Rams are 7-3 ATS in their last 10 against Washington, which ranks 31st in opponent rush success rate and has Terry McLaurin on IR.

NYG@PHI.text: Joe Milton III becomes the Eagles' third starting QB this season with Jalen Hurts on IR. Philly has lost six straight, so no pressure, Joe.

NYJ@KC.text: The Chiefs were 5-0 a few weeks ago; now they've lost two straight, with Kenneth Walker averaging 2.6 and 3.3 yards per carry in them.

HOU@LAC.text: The Chargers are 0-7 straight up and 0-6-1 against the spread. Not a single cover all year. Impressive, in its own way.

LV@SF.text: Kirk Cousins has 19 TD passes and the Raiders are 6-2 against the spread. Yes, those Raiders.

ARI@SEA.text: Sam Darnold is out (quad), so Drew Lock likely starts. Lock threw three TD passes at Arizona in Week 2. The Cards remember.

GB@NE.text: The Under is 5-0 in Green Bay's last five games. The Over is 5-0 in New England's last five. Something has to give.

TB@CHI.text: The Bucs blanked Atlanta 16-0 without completing a single pass. Bucky Irving's 728 rushing yards: apparently all you need.

BUF@MIN.text: Kyler Murray is out with a hamstring strain, so Carson Wentz starts for the 6-1 Vikings, and the line slid toward Buffalo. Bring it, Carson.

WAS@NYG.text: Round one ended in a tie because Washington ran out of clock in overtime. Meanwhile, the Giants have covered six of eight.

NE@DET.text: The Patriots' last six games all went Over, but the last three Pats-Lions meetings all went Under. One streak dies in Munich.

BUF@NYJ.text: The Bills are 5-0 ATS in their last five against the Jets, who've given up 26+ points in four straight losses. Rough neighborhood.

CAR@NO.text: Chase Young has eight sacks in eight games and a sack in three straight. Carolina's QB may want to get rid of it early.

HOU@CLE.text: The Texans are 0-4 at home and 3-1 on the road. The Browns are 3-0 at home, winning every one as underdogs. Something's gotta give.

JAX@TEN.text: The 1-7 Titans still haven't won at home, and Jacksonville has won and covered four straight in this series.

KC@ATL.text: Patrick Mahomes's elbow MRI showed no major injury, and he's expected to play. 92% of DraftKings bets are on KC. Falcons, take it personally.

MIA@IND.text: Malik Willis is on IR, so Kyle McCord lines up for his first start without a single NFL regular-season pass. Welcome to Indy, rook.

MIN@GB.text: With Kyler Murray's hamstring strain, Minnesota traded for Kirk Cousins, who's likely to start at Lambeau. Only 34% of spread bets trust it.

LA@ARI.text: Arizona is down to third-string QB Carson Beck for his first NFL start, and the Rams list Puka Nacua as doubtful. Buckle up.

SEA@LV.text: Vegas shipped Kirk Cousins out, so Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza makes his first NFL start. The total promptly dropped from 43 to 40.5.

SF@DAL.text: The 49ers have covered the last four meetings, and the Over has hit in six of nine Cowboys games. Bring snacks, not defense.

PIT@CIN.text: Both are 6-2 and the winner owns the AFC North. Joe Burrow leads all QBs with 23 TD passes. Pittsburgh's secondary is on notice.

LAC@BAL.text: The 0-8 Chargers are 0-7-1 against the spread, and the Ravens are 2-7 ATS. Somebody has to cover on Monday night. Probably.
